findings.title: Local Development Credential: Database Connection URI
findings.description: Connection string points to a local development or loopback service (e.g. localhost, 127.0.0.1).
findings.remediation: Ensure production environments do not rely on hardcoded local configuration values.

findings.title: AWS Access Key ID
findings.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS) Access Key ID detected.
findings.remediation: Deactivate and delete the exposed AWS access key via the AWS IAM Console immediately. Use IAM Roles or AWS Secrets Manager instead.

findings.title: AWS Secret Access Key
findings.description: AWS Secret Access Key assignment detected.
findings.remediation: Rotate the secret access key immediately. Migrate to temporary credentials via AWS STS or IAM Instance Profiles.

findings.title: GitHub Personal Access Token
findings.description: GitHub Personal Access Token (classic or fine-grained) or OAuth token detected.
findings.remediation: Revoke the token immediately from your GitHub Account Settings -> Developer settings -> Personal access tokens. Restrict permissions using fine-grained scopes.

findings.title: RSA Private Key
findings.description: Unencrypted RSA private cryptographic key detected in source code.
findings.remediation: Remove the private key from the codebase, revoke and rotate the corresponding keypair, and inject keys dynamically via secret vaults (e.g., HashiCorp Vault, AWS KMS).

findings.title: High-Entropy Suspicious Credential
findings.description: Variable assignment contains a string with high Shannon entropy (4.66), indicating a machine-generated secret or key.
findings.remediation: Verify whether this high-randomness string is an active credential. Externalize to environment variables or secret vaults.

findings.title: OpenAI API Key
findings.remediation: Revoke the key in the OpenAI API dashboard. Use environment variables to pass API keys at runtime.

findings.remediation: Externalize API keys and secret tokens into environment configurations or a secrets manager.
